chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The dinner of the Prophets (peace be upon them) is after 'atamah (late night/dusk), so do not neglect it, for neglecting the dinner is the ruin of the body.'

key_terms.الْعَتَمَة: Late night or deep dusk (time after Maghrib/Isha)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of eating dinner late at night according to the Prophets?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic tradition of consuming the main meal late at night, a practice linked to maintaining physical vitality and preventing bodily decay. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted not merely as a dietary habit but as a means of aligning with the Sunnah of the Prophet and the Imams, emphasizing the balance between spiritual discipline and physical health. The advice to not neglect this meal underscores the importance of sustaining the body as an amanah (trust) from God.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from the grandfather of Al Hassan Bin Rashid, form Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The dinner of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> was after the darkness, therefore do not leave it. So if you were to neglect the dinner, the body would be ruined’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hassan ibn Rashid from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said,
’Dinner of the Prophets is after al-’Atmah (the time of late evening Salat (prayer)); so you must not ignore dinner because ignoring it leads to neglecting the body.”’
